heading: CSV to Markdown Table
subtitle: Drop a CSV and get a Markdown table at once, ready to paste into GitHub, Notion or Obsidian.
intro: Put a spreadsheet into a README, a pull request, a wiki page or your notes without lining up pipes by hand. Choose, drop or paste a CSV or TSV file and a GitHub-flavoured Markdown table appears at once: the header row, the --- separator line, then one line per row. A | inside a cell is escaped so it does not split the column. The table renders in GitHub, GitLab, Notion and Obsidian. The delimiter and encoding are detected for you, and the file is read in your browser, never uploaded.

handlesTitle: What the CSV to Markdown converter handles
handles: Files: .csv and .tsv, or CSV text you paste; comma, semicolon, tab and pipe delimiters.
Encodings: UTF-8, UTF-16 (when the file starts with a byte order mark), Windows-1256 Arabic and Windows-1252 Western European text, detected automatically.
Output: a GitHub-flavoured table with a header row and a --- separator line.
A | inside a cell escaped as \|, so it stays in its column.
Tables that render in GitHub, GitLab, Notion, Obsidian and other Markdown editors.

faqTitle: CSV to Markdown: questions and answers

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. The CSV is read and turned into a Markdown table by your browser, on your device. Pasted text stays in this tab and is never sent anywhere.

faq.question: Where does the table render?
faq.answer: Anywhere that reads GitHub-flavoured Markdown tables: GitHub and GitLab READMEs, issues and pull requests, Notion, Obsidian and most Markdown editors.

faq.question: What happens to a | inside a cell?
faq.answer: It is written as \| so the table reader sees it as text, not as a column border, and the row keeps its columns.

faq.question: Can a cell hold several lines?
faq.answer:
A Markdown table has one line per row, so a line break inside a cell is written as
, which most Markdown viewers show as a new line.

faq.question: My CSV uses semicolons. Will it work?
faq.answer: Yes. The delimiter is detected from the file, whether it is a comma, semicolon, tab or pipe, so CSV files saved by Excel in Europe convert too.

faq.question: Can I edit the CSV before converting?
faq.answer: Yes: open it in the CSV viewer, edit the cells and save, then convert the saved file to Markdown.

faq.question: How do I convert a CSV file to a Markdown table?
faq.answer: Open or paste the CSV: the first row becomes the header, followed by one Markdown line per row, ready to copy into a README or download as a .md file. OpenAnyDoc converts it in your browser, without uploading the data.
